annotations.text:
Why there is no staged status line.

generateTickets() in src/lib/actions/generate.ts is one blocking server action: auth, read North Star, read live tickets, ONE non-streaming chat.completions.create, log, validate, insert, supersede. The client observes exactly two things — pending true, then pending false with a message. There is no stream and no progress event, so "Reading your North Star… Sequencing 9 tickets…" would be invented, and the ticket count is not known until the model has already returned.

What the wait shows instead is true at the moment it is painted: the .ai-dot (the AI is working), the 10-30s expectation from the current button copy, the elapsed seconds (the client's own timer), and a static summary of what actually went into the prompt. "Up to 10 tickets" is the system prompt's own cap, not a guess.

Past 30s the working line changes once — "Still working. This is slower than usual." — and nothing else moves. That is honest: elapsed time is the only thing the client can measure. No percentage, no fake stage advance, no spinner that implies a known duration.

The entrance, frozen.

design.md §2 gives a new object taking a slot ~250ms of fade + 8px slide-up, and §1 rules out sequenced motion — so this is TWO objects arriving, the rail list and the focus card, not nine staggered rows. Both artboards freeze at ~170ms (opacity .78, 2px of the 8px left to travel). The Motion tweak flips to 'settled' to compare against the resting frame.

SYN-001, not SYN-004, holds the Focus slot here. This is the first generation, so nothing is done, and queue.ts only surfaces a ticket whose depends_on are all done. SYN-004 depends on SYN-003; it cannot be current until three tickets are finished. Everything behind the two dependency-free tickets carries the dashed waiting ring.

The rail stays truthful while a regeneration is in flight.

superseded_at is stamped LAST in generate.ts — after the insert succeeds — precisely so a failed call cannot leave the user with nothing to work on. So during a regeneration all nine tickets are still live: the count line still reads 3 of 9 done, 1 blocked, and the progress bar does not move. The 45% fade on the Now and Up next rows is a preview of what this action will retire, not a claim that it already has. Blocked and Done stay at full opacity because they genuinely survive.

Status appears where the trigger was. The stall card's .btn-primary keeps its status in the card (1); the rail footer's .btn-outline keeps its confirmation, its working state and its error in the rail footer (3, 4, 5). Both triggers share one pending state, so the other one goes .is-disabled rather than staying clickable.

Failure, in the §3 inline-error recipe: peach-soft ground, peach-text, alert glyph, --radius-sm, never a modal or a toast. The human sentence leads and says what survives (design.md §5); the raw model string is demoted into a detail well below it, because it is the only thing worth pasting into a bug report.

The rail is fully restored — solid rows, unchanged counts — and its footer returns to the ordinary Regenerate queue button with a compact .err line above it, so both triggers work again.

The 503 string is sample text in the shape Gemini actually returns; swap it for the real error.message.
